name: Airlines (regional and low-cost operations)

problems.words: Domestic sectors fly half empty midweek
quick_ideas: Put last month's loads by route and weekday side by side once, so the weak days are seen rather than felt
Ask counter and call-centre staff which midweek routes people ask about but don't book, so you learn the reason behind the gap.

workzap_build.text: a morning read on the owner's WhatsApp every day showing load, revenue and ancillaries per flight, with the weakest midweek sectors flagged automatically across the whole network.

problems.ask_first: Is it a few routes every midweek, or most domestic sectors?
problems.free_stops: How to set load thresholds per route and act on them is worked out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note last week's booked seats for each domestic midweek sector beside weekend sectors, so the weaker days stand out route by route.
Give one commercial staff member the job of reviewing midweek domestic loads every Tuesday, so quiet sectors get attention before departure.

problems.words: Route profit is unknown after fuel and leases
quick_ideas: Work out one month's profit for your single busiest route by hand, so you see which cost line moves the result most
Get commercial and finance to agree which costs belong to a route, so everyone argues from the same list.

workzap_build.text: a route profitability view that updates daily, combining ticket and ancillary revenue with fuel, lease, handling and catering cost per sector, converted to one currency.

problems.ask_first: Which cost hurts most today, fuel, leases or handling?
problems.free_stops: How each shared cost is split across routes is set out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Write one busy route's income and main route costs on one page for last month, so the biggest margin guesswork shows.
Make one finance person keep the route cost list in one notebook, so commercial and finance use the same basis each week.

problems.words: GSAs abroad remit late and their figures never match ours
quick_ideas: List every GSA with amount owed and days outstanding once, so you know who to chase first
Name one person in finance who owns the GSA check, so mismatches stop falling between teams.

workzap_build.text: a settlement tracker that matches agent sales, BSP statements and receipts every day, ages each balance and sends reminders on schedule.

problems.ask_first: Is the bigger problem the delay itself, or the figures not matching?
problems.free_stops: The matching rules and reminder schedule are kept for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare one recent GSA remittance advice with your own sales summary for the same period, so the mismatch point appears quickly.
Give one finance person one running list of each GSA mismatch and reply date, so follow up stays with one owner.

quick_ideas: Count your open refunds once and note where each is stuck, so you see which stage is the bottleneck
Give the oldest ones to a named person, so someone owns them.

workzap_build.text: a refund pipeline where every request shows stage, age and owner, and the passenger is updated automatically each time it moves.

problems.ask_first: Where does a refund usually get stuck, approval, accounts or payout?
problems.free_stops: The stages, owners and passenger update points are designed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count open cancellation refunds by where they are waiting right now, so the slowest handover point becomes visible.
Give one person the daily refund holding list and a fixed review time, so stalled cases are chased without delay.

problems.words: Every delay brings a flood of calls and WhatsApps
quick_ideas: Decide who sends updates during a disruption, so outbound messages don't compete with inbound calls
Check after your next delay how many calls came from passengers who simply hadn't heard, so you know the size of the gap.

workzap_build.text: a disruption flow that notifies every affected booking automatically (contacts used with passengers' permission) and offers a rebooking or refund request link, with response counts tracked.

problems.ask_first: Do most bookings carry a mobile number today?
problems.free_stops: The message flow and rebooking link setup are part of the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: After the next delay, note how many calls and messages arrived before any update went out, so silence costs become clear.
Assign one duty person to send delay updates at fixed moments, so inbound traffic eases when passengers hear from you early.

quick_ideas: Make one booking on a phone yourself and note where extras are offered, so you see what passengers see
Ask check-in staff which extras people ask for at the airport, so you know what demand exists.

workzap_build.text: a post-booking page and WhatsApp link where passengers add bags, seats or meals at any time, with ancillary sales reported per route each day.

problems.ask_first: Do most passengers book on your website or through agents?
problems.free_stops: Where and when extras are offered in the journey is set out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Watch today's bookings and note which extras are actually added before payment, so weak ancillary points are easier to spot.
Give one airport staff member one list of extras passengers ask for most, so sales ideas come from real requests.

quick_ideas: Try a few test bookings on different phones and banks and note where each fails, so you know if it's one cause or several
Ask your payment provider for last week's declined attempts, so you see how many sales are leaking.

workzap_build.text: a booking and payment flow connected to your reservation system, with every failed payment flagged to sales for follow-up the same day.

problems.ask_first: Does it fail on certain cards or banks, or for everyone?
problems.free_stops: The fix itself and the follow-up flow are scoped in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Try bookings from different phones on the same route and note the exact payment break point, so the common failure point is clear.
Give one person one page for every payment break report this week, so patterns stop being scattered across chats.

problems.words: Crew roster built in Excel, changes go out on WhatsApp
quick_ideas: Agree that one shared roster is the only current version, so nobody works from an old copy
Ask crew to confirm the latest change they received, so you see who is missing updates.

workzap_build.text: a roster publishing tool where every change reaches the affected roles and needs an acknowledgement, with per diems calculated from the final roster for payroll (duty limits stay with your ops team).

problems.ask_first: Is the main pain the publishing, or the allowance calculation afterwards?
problems.free_stops: The acknowledgement flow and allowance rules are kept for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare the latest roster change notice with what crew supervisors say is current, so you see how often versions drift apart.
Name one operations person to post every roster change in one chat thread, so crews stop checking multiple places.

problems.words: Station managers report on their own phones, no common format
quick_ideas: Agree with station managers the four or five things they report each day, so reports become comparable
Collect them in one place instead of private chats, so nothing is lost.

workzap_build.text: a phone form each outstation fills daily, rolled into one view at base every morning with missing reports flagged.

problems.ask_first: How many outstations report to you today?
problems.free_stops: The form fields and the base view layout are designed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Look at yesterday's station reports side by side and note which key operating facts are missing most often, so weak reporting habits show.
Give one duty manager one shared reporting time for all stations each day, so updates arrive together and comparisons are easier.

problems.words: Ground handling invoices higher than agreed
quick_ideas: Check one recent invoice from your busiest outstation against the agreed rate card, so you know if the gap is rates or services
Gather all stations' rate cards in one place, so checks are possible at all.

workzap_build.text: an invoice checker that compares every handling bill with the station's rate card and logged services, flagging differences before payment across all stations.

problems.ask_first: Are the differences in rates, or in services you don't recognise?
problems.free_stops: The checking rules per station are worked out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare one disputed handling invoice line by line with the agreed station rate card, so overcharges split into rates versus extra services.
Give one finance person one notebook page for disputed station charges, so every query and supplier reply sits together until cleared.

never_say: Anything about airworthiness, maintenance release, MEL items, flight or duty-time limits, crew licensing or safety management; those belong to the accountable managers and the regulator.
Any reading of PCAA, GCAA or Transport Canada rules, or ways around slot, route or permit rules.
Fuel hedging, lease, tax or employment-law advice; suggest they talk to their financial adviser, accountant or lawyer.
Anything that helps alter load sheets, crew hours, logbooks or maintenance records.
Comments on competitor airlines or individuals in incidents, and any storage of passenger or crew names, PNRs or passport data.

sample_reply.person: Every time a flight is delayed our call centre gets buried and passengers still find out at the airport. Can you suggest a fix?
sample_reply.pi: Yes, this can be improved, and it starts with who tells passengers first. 1. Decide one person who sends updates during a disruption, so outbound news isn't stuck behind incoming calls. 2. After the next delay, check how many callers simply hadn't been told, so you know how big the gap is. Workzap can do this automatically for you: every affected booking gets notified the moment a delay is entered, with the passenger's permission, plus a link to request rebooking or a refund. Shall I put together a solution document and quote for you? You're free to say no.
